exposure: isolated abdominal circumference < 10th percentile for gestational age (GA) (iAC group)
overall estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile (EFW group)
cohort: 635 singleton pregnancies with growth ultrasounds at a single health system
finding: Diagnosing fetal growth restriction (FGR) based on isolated abdominal circumference < 10th percentile led to a higher number of FGR cases but was associated with better obstetric and neonatal outcomes compared to using estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile.
mod_finding: Isolated abdominal circumference < 10th percentile for gestational age (iAC) as a definition of fetal growth restriction (FGR) was associated with lower rates of preterm birth compared to using overall estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile as a definition of FGR.
